cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.title: High-Contrast Card Focus
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.objective: Support visual focus with one bold black-and-white card.
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.description: Baby looks at a single high-contrast card held 8–12 inches away while you describe the pattern.
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.preparation:
Select one simple pattern (stripes or bullseye)
Sit facing baby
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.setup: Baby comfortable on mat; card ready.
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.steps:
1. Hold card steady in view
2. Allow time to focus
3. Move slightly side to side
4. Name pattern simply (stripes/spots)
5. Rest eyes
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.safetyNotes: Sealed laminate edges; no glitter/loose parts.
teacherTips: One card at a time; put extras away.
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.imageBriefSetup: Caregiver holding one bold B/W stripe card 8–12 inches from infant.

cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.title: Tummy Time Pattern Line
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.objective: Invite head lifting toward a tummy-time contrast strip.
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.description: During supervised tummy time, a printable contrast strip sits at eye level in front of baby.
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.materials:
Tummy-time visual strip (printable)
Mat
Optional support roll
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.preparation: Place strip along front edge of mat
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.setup: Awake tummy time facing the strip.
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.steps:
1. Place baby on tummy
2. Point to a pattern on the strip
3. Get face-to-face beside strip
4. Encourage looking/lifting
5. Rest on back
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.teacherLanguage: You are looking at the bold patterns!
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.safetyNotes: Awake and supervised only; back to sleep.
teacherTips: Your face beside the strip doubles engagement.
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.imageBriefSetup: Tummy-time mat with B/W visual strip at infant eye level.

cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.title: Mirror and Pattern Meet
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.objective: Alternate looking at a baby-safe mirror and a contrast card.
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.description: Baby looks in a mirror, then at a nearby high-contrast card, with your narration linking both.
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.setup: Mirror and card side by side on mat edge.
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.steps:
1. Show mirror first
2. Point to baby’s face
3. Show contrast card
4. Return to mirror
5. Smile and close
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.teacherLanguage: I see your face — and a bold pattern too.
teacherTips: Faces still win — keep card secondary.
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.imageBriefSetup: Baby-safe mirror beside one B/W card on mat.

cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.title: Bold Card Gaze Garden
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.objective: Offer a calm sequence of 2–3 contrast cards for gazing.
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.description: You present one card at a time in a quiet ‘garden’ of visuals, watching for focus and break cues.
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.preparation: Order cards from simplest to busier
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.setup: Sit with cards face down; show one at a time.
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.steps:
1. Show card 1 still
2. Allow gaze
3. Switch to card 2
4. Optional card 3 if still alert
5. Stop at first fatigue cue
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.observationOpportunities: Maintains calm alert looking; switches attention.
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.safetyNotes: No card stacks within baby’s kick zone as clutter.
teacherTips: Gaze aversion means break, not ‘try harder’.
observationPrompts: Maintains calm alert looking; switches attention.

cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.title: Black White Board Book
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.objective: Share a high-contrast board book page by page.
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.description: Short read-aloud focusing on one bold page with slow pointing.
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.steps:
1. Open to bold page
2. Point to a shape
3. Say black/white
4. Turn one page if interested
5. Close gently
teacherTips: Silence between words helps looking.

cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.title: Contrast Card Peek Song
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.objective: Play a gentle peek game with a contrast card and song.
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.description: You hide a card briefly behind your hand, reveal it with a smile, and sing a short peek phrase.
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.steps:
1. Show card
2. Hide behind hand
3. Sing peek phrase
4. Reveal with smile
5. Repeat once or twice
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.safetyNotes: No sudden loud peeks for sensitive infants.
teacherTips: Your face reveal can replace the card sometimes.

cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.title: Slow Pattern Arc Track
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.objective: Practice eye tracking along a slow arc with a contrast card.
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.description: Move a patterned card in a slow left–center–right arc while baby watches.
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.setup: Baby on back; card in starting left position.
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.steps:
1. Gain attention on card
2. Move slowly left to center
3. Pause
4. Move slowly to right
5. Rest card still
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.observationOpportunities: Eyes follow arc; refocuses at pause.
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.safetyNotes: Stop if eyes fatigue or baby fussing.
teacherTips: If baby loses track, shorten the arc.
observationPrompts: Eyes follow arc; refocuses at pause.
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.imageBriefSetup: Caregiver moving B/W card in slow arc above infant on back.

cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.title: Tummy Contrast Gallery
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.objective: Offer 2 contrast visuals during tummy time without clutter.
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.description: Two cards stand along the mat edge like a tiny gallery while baby does tummy time.
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.preparation:
Space cards apart
Sit opposite baby
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.steps:
1. Place baby on tummy
2. Tap lightly near one card to invite look
3. Shift attention to second card
4. Return to face-to-face
5. Rest
teacherTips: Two visuals max.
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.imageBriefSetup: Two B/W cards propped at mat edge for tummy time.

cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.title: Black White Cloth Look
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.objective: Explore a large black/white cloth with eyes and hands — never as a face cover.
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.description: A large contrast cloth is shown and offered for touch while you hold it; it is never draped over baby’s face.
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.setup: Hold cloth on your hands in baby’s view.
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.steps:
1. Show cloth open
2. Crinkle gently for sound if fabric allows
3. Offer edge for touch
4. Name black and white
5. Fold away
teacherTips: Rename activity away from ‘drape’ to avoid unsafe setups.

substitutions.use: hold cloth on adult hands only

cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.imageBriefSetup: Caregiver holding open B/W cloth on hands near infant — not covering infant.

cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.title: Zebra Stripe Soft Book
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.objective: Touch stripes in a soft high-contrast book with narration.
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.description: Guide hands over striped soft-book pages while naming stripe and pattern.
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.steps:
1. Open soft book
2. Guide hand over stripes
3. Name stripe
4. Crinkle page if present
5. Cuddle to finish
teacherTips: Hand-over-hand lightly — follow baby’s pressure.

cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.title: Grasp the Contrast Ring
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.ageModifications: Often ~3–6 months; younger may only look
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.objective: Offer a large high-contrast ring for looking and grasping when ready.
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.description: A large soft black/white ring is presented for visual attention and optional grasp.
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.preparation:
Sanitize ring
Confirm size too large to choke
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.setup: Baby on back or supported semi-reclined.
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.steps:
1. Show ring still
2. Move slightly to invite look
3. Bring within reach
4. Allow grasp if baby closes fingers
5. Celebrate any contact
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.safetyNotes: Large ring only; supervised mouthing; no cords.
teacherTips: Looking-only is a full success for younger infants.
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.imageBriefSetup: Large B/W ring offered within infant reach on mat.

cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.title: Hello Black Hello White
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.objective: Greet each baby with the original hello song and a face or pattern card.
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.description: Personal hello using song while alternating your face and a simple face/pattern card.
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.steps:
1. Eye contact
2. Show face card
3. Sing hello lines
4. Lower card; show your face
5. Cuddle close
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.observationOpportunities: Social smile/coo; looks at card and face.
teacherTips: Alternate card and real face — real face is the goal.
observationPrompts: Social smile/coo; looks at card and face.

cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.title: Contrast Celebration Hold
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.objective: Celebrate the week with a gentle sway and favorite contrast card.
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.description: Secure hold with soft sway while showing a favorite pattern card and humming.
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.setup: Secure hold; card in peripheral view.
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.steps:
1. Hold securely
2. Show favorite card
3. Hum or sing short line
4. Slow sway
5. Stillness and smile
teacherTips: Celebration can be quiet.

cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.title: Favorite Pattern Page Party
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.objective: Revisit a favorite high-contrast page as a week closing ritual.
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.description: Short party atmosphere (soft cheer) around one favorite book page or card.
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.preparation: Know each baby’s preferred visual if observed
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.setup: Lap or small group with one visual.
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.steps:
1. Show favorite page/card
2. Name what baby liked (stripes/face)
3. Soft cheer
4. One more look
5. Put away for next week
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.safetyNotes: Keep cheers soft for sensitive infants.
teacherTips: Document preferences for families.

cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.title: Shade and Shadow Contrast Stroll
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.objective: Notice natural light/dark contrast outdoors with caregiver talk.
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.description: In safe shade, point out shadows and bright/dark areas while strolling or sitting.
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.materials:
Stroller or blanket
Optional contrast card
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.steps:
1. Settle baby
2. Point to shadow/light area
3. Describe dark and light
4. Optional show card in outdoor light
5. Return inside
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.observationOpportunities: Looks toward pointed contrast; content outdoors.
cur-lp-infant-black-white-discovery:item.safetyNotes: Shade; supervision; safe sleep if drowsy.
teacherTips: Natural contrast is powerful — keep it simple.
observationPrompts: Looks toward pointed contrast; content outdoors.

week.weeklyOverview: High-contrast black-and-white patterns support early visual focus and tracking. The week centers on looking, tummy-time visuals, faces, short books, songs, and caregiver talk — not crafts or worksheets.
week.objectives:
Strengthen visual focus with simple high-contrast patterns
Practice slow tracking of bold cards/objects
Support tummy-time looking with contrast visuals
Use face cards and caregiver faces as primary targets
Offer safe reaching toward large contrast toys when ready
week.weeklyMaterials:
High-contrast pattern cards (printable draft)
Face cards (printable draft)
Tummy-time visual strip (printable draft)
High-contrast board/soft books
Baby-safe mirror
Black/white fabric squares
Large soft contrast ring/toy
week.familyConnection: Share that simple black-and-white cards during alert awake time can support looking — always with your face and voice.
week.adaptations: Younger infants need closer (8–12 in), slower moves, fewer cards. Reduce if overstimulated. Older infants may reach for large contrast toys.
week.vocabularyWords:
look
see
black
white
pattern
stripe
spot
face
watch
focus
week.teacherPreparation:
Print/laminate draft contrast cards and face cards
Stage tummy-time strip on mat edge
Sanitize soft books and ring toys

songs.lyrics:
Hello black, hello white,
I see patterns day and night.
Hello face, hello you,
Looking, looking, we do too.

prepChecklist: Set calm mat with one visual at a time
Check mirror and soft book condition
observationFocus: Gaze duration on contrast vs face
teacherToolkit.teacherPreparation: Present one pattern at a time. Your face remains the richest visual.
teacherToolkit.notes: Printables are draft visuals for attention — not worksheets.
